Say yes to something — Estar de acuerdo / aceptar.
We all agreed to the new plan.
v|Beside consent and coincide. Patterns: agree with someone, agree to a plan, agree that.
She lives alone in the country.
The ticket alone cost fifty euros.
Beside solitary. Careful: alone is a fact, lonely is a feeling.
How much there is of something — Cantidad.
A small amount of sugar is enough.
Add up to a total — Ascender a / sumar.
The bill amounts to eighty euros.
v|Beside quantity. Amount is for uncountable things, number for countable ones.
He answered my question at once.
I am still waiting for an answer.
v|Beside respond. The w is silent.
Worried about what may happen — Ansioso/a / inquieto/a.
She felt anxious before the exam.
Very keen to do something — Deseoso/a / con ganas.
He is anxious to meet you.
Showing that you think something is good — De aprobación / aprobatorio/a.
Beside sympathetic. Verb: approve. Opposite: disapproving.
Want very much to reach something high — Aspirar a.
He aspires to be a doctor.
v|Beside soar. Patterns: aspire to something, aspire to do something.
A person you work with — Socio/a / colega.
He is a business associate of mine.
Connect two things in your mind — Asociar / relacionar.
I associate that song with summer.
v|Beside colleague. The noun ends in a soft -at, the verb in -eit.
The power of pulling someone towards something — Atracción.
The attraction of city life is the work.
Something people come to see — Atracción / punto de interés.
The castle is the town's main attraction.
Ordinary; neither good nor bad — Medio/a / corriente.
The number found by adding and dividing — Promedio / media.
v|Beside commence. Patterns: begin to do and begin doing.
It was brave of her to speak up.
Beside gallant and valiant. Noun: bravery. Adverb: bravely.
He was given a medal for bravery.
A machine or system failing — Avería / fallo.
We had a breakdown on the motorway.
A collapse of health or talks — Crisis / ruptura.
The talks ended in a breakdown.
Beside collapse. From the phrasal verb break down.
The work a person does to earn money — Negocio / ocupación.
What line of business are you in?
Beside vocation. Note the spelling: busi-ness, said BIZ-nis.
Buy something you sold before — Recomprar / volver a comprar.
The company bought back its own shares.
v|Beside redeem. Separable: buy it back.
Quiet and not upset — Tranquilo/a / sereno/a.
v|Beside soothe. The l is silent.
Not taking enough care — Descuidado/a / negligente.
One careless mistake lost the game.
Beside reckless and heedless. Opposite: careful. Noun: carelessness.
I am certain I locked the door.
Particular but not named — Cierto/a / determinado/a.
Beside confident. Adverb: certainly. Noun: certainty.
The town has changed a lot.
Money given back, noun — Cambio / vuelto.
Easy to see through — Transparente / claro/a.
Quick to learn and understand — Listo/a / inteligente.
Showing skill or new thinking — Ingenioso/a.
Beside ingenious and innovative. Adverb: cleverly.
Moving awkwardly and dropping things — Torpe.
He is too clumsy to carry the glasses.
Appear or become visible — Salir / aparecer.
The stars came out after sunset.
Become known — Salir a la luz / saberse.
Make someone feel better — Consolar / reconfortar.
A pleasant easy state, noun — Comodidad / bienestar.
Having every part; whole — Completo/a / íntegro/a.
Make someone unable to think clearly — Confundir / desconcertar.
People often confuse the two brothers.
Defeating and taking control — Conquistador(a) / vencedor(a).
The conquering army entered the city.
Beside victorious. Verb: conquer, said KON-ker. Noun: conquest.
v|Beside amend. Adverb: correctly. Noun: correction.
Brave in the face of danger — Valeroso/a / valiente.
Beside valiant. Noun: courage. Adverb: courageously.
The person who made or invented something — Creador(a).
She is the creator of the series.
Beside architect. Verb: create. Noun: creation.
Person who breaks the law — Delincuente / criminal.
The criminal was caught that night.
Beside delinquent and outlaw. Noun: crime.
Damage something so it cannot work — Paralizar / inutilizar.
v|Beside maim. Used of a person it is offensive now; say disable or injure instead.
Draw a line through writing to cancel it — Tachar.
v|Beside cancel. Separable: cross it out.
It is cruel to leave a dog alone all day.
Beside brutal and vicious. Noun: cruelty. Adverb: cruelly.
Person who buys from a shop or business — Cliente/a.
Beside client. A client usually pays for a service, a customer buys goods.
The chance that something bad will happen — Peligro.
There is a danger of flooding.
Beside peril. Adjective: dangerous. Phrase: in danger.
With little or no light — Oscuro/a.
The room was dark and cold.
Those were dark days for the town.
Beside gloomy and dismal. Noun: darkness.
The snake has a deadly bite.
Beside mortal. Careful: deadly is an adjective, deathly means like death.
Choose what to do after thinking — Decidir.
We decided to stay at home.
v|Beside conclude. Noun: decision. Pattern: decide to do something.
Choose one thing from several — Decidirse por / optar por.
They decided on the blue one.
Beside final. Phrase: the deciding factor.
Make something happen later — Retrasar / demorar.
Easily broken or damaged — Delicado/a / frágil.
Say what someone or something is like — Describir.
Can you describe the man you saw?
v|Beside perish. Forms: dies, died, died; the -ing form is dying.
Take something out of the ground — Desenterrar / sacar.
They dug up the old pipes.
Find out hidden information — Sacar a la luz / desenterrar.
The reporter dug up the whole story.
v|Beside unearth. Separable: dig it up.
Calm and serious in a way that earns respect — Digno/a / solemne.
Not bright; hard to see — Tenue / débil.
A dim light came from the hall.
Beside gloomy. Comparative: dimmer. Verb: dim the lights.
Going straight, with nothing in between — Directo/a.
Saying plainly what you mean — Directo/a / franco/a.
Make something stop working — Desactivar / inutilizar.
Take away someone's physical ability — Discapacitar / incapacitar.
The accident disabled him for life.
Not having the same opinion — Desacuerdo / discrepancia.
There was disagreement about the price.
Beside conflict. Verb: disagree. Opposite: agreement.
Show something where people can see it — Exponer / exhibir.
The shop displays cakes in the window.
A show or arrangement, noun — Exposición / muestra.
There was a display of old photographs.
Pay no attention to something — Hacer caso omiso de / desatender.
She looked disturbed by the question.
Beside uneasy. Also used of serious mental distress, so choose the word with care.
The river dries up every August.
Funding for the project dried up.
v|Beside scorch. Not separable in these senses.
The state of having no water or rain — Sequedad / aridez.
The dryness of the air cracked her lips.
Live in a place — Morar / habitar.
Few people dwell on the island now.
Keep thinking or talking about something — Darle vueltas a / detenerse en.
Do not dwell on your mistakes.
v|Beside abide and inhabit. Formal or literary. Pattern: dwell on something.
